newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street open seen mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street open seen mixed to higher.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open mixed to higher Wednesday, with investors focusing on U.S. inflation data and patent infringement suits against Intel Corp.

If Producer Price Index figures, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, come in as expected or lower, U.S. stocks could rally on hopes that the Federal Open Market Committee will leave interest rates unchanged at its meeting next Tuesday, analysts said.

"If the core (PPI) rate comes in within expectations or slightly less, the market should make up yesterday's losses or ... (get) closer to new high territory," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
A consensus estimate by economists calls for April PPI to be unchanged. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, core PPI is expected to rise 0.1 percent.

Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said Wall Street could open mixed on worries spawned by patent infringement suits against Intel by Cyrix Corp and Digital Equipment Corp.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 10 points Tuesday, led by sharp losses in Intel. The semiconductor maker's stock fell 6-3/4 to 152-3/8 in heavy trade.
"We'll probably get a mixed opening because of this confusion, and then I think we'll work back to the plus side," Brown said.
Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average closed up 80.61 points, or 0.40 percent, at 20,209.72.
In London the FTSE 100 was down 25.9 at 4665.1, and U.S. stocks were narrowly mixed.
The dollar was higher against the yen in Tokyo at 118.83/93 and was at 1.7064/74 against the mark in Europe.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 3/32 to yield 6.92 percent, and the Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 0.50 to 838.35.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said International Business Machines Corp touched an intraday high Tuesday at 177-1/8, a mark last hit in August 1987. The stock closed up 1/8 at 173-5/8.

The New York Times's Market Place column said IBM's intraday high came in a far different market than that of a decade ago. IBM is only ninth among U.S. companies in market value, down from No. 1 in 1987, and ranks third among technology companies.
